answer: Topological Cut-Cost Pricing. Each identity must maintain outbound links to agents that independently route traffic through it; a link only counts if the neighbor's topology differs from yours, measured as graph edit distance, so a sybil cluster mirroring one shape earns no credit. Pricing sits on the cut between link-disjoint neighbor sets, likened to water draining a karst: flow disperses only through distinct channels, and a dense knoll of clustered fakes cannot pool.
